added_lemmas.justification: This removes exponential support expansion for completely randomized designs while preserving ordinary midranks and equality faces.
added_lemmas.gap: Li--Sheng--Yu obtain a closed form under index-resolved tie-breaking, whereas the explicit-row leaf evaluator would enumerate all completely randomized assignments; the coefficient dynamic program evaluates each ordinary-midrank leaf from a succinct design.
added_lemmas.consumer: Analysts facing arbitrary fixed treatment-indexed attrition under complete randomization can compute the exact robust tail in polynomial time for every fixed number of missing outcomes.

proposed_core_edits.name: bitsCRE
proposed_core_edits.reason: The succinct completely randomized-design algorithm must measure an input that does not contain the exponentially large assignment list counted by the existing explicit-support length.

proposed.name: bitsCRE
proposed.def: \(\ell_{\mathrm{CRE}}\) is the total binary encoding length of \(n\), \(m\), \(a\), the rational value \(\delta\), and the labeled rational partial vector \(y^{\mathrm{obs},\delta}\), when \(\Omega=\mathcal Z_m\) and \(w_z=\binom{n}{m}^{-1}\) are supplied as a succinct completely randomized-design promise rather than as an explicit row list.

prose_updates.tldr: Attrition makes both a rank statistic and its randomization reference tail depend on missing sharp-null outcomes. For an explicitly listed rationally weighted fixed-count design, the exact worst-case Wilcoxon-midrank p-value is the maximum over a finite complex of complete weak orders, including equality faces. The envelope is finite-sample valid under arbitrary fixed treatment-indexed observation, computable in \(O((2n+1)^k n|\Omega|\operatorname{poly}(\ell))\) time with a linear one-missing sweep, invertible over additive effects by a finite breakpoint scan, and NP-complete to maximize when \(k\) varies. For a succinct completely randomized design, the same ordinary-midrank maximum is computable in \(\left[\prod_{j=0}^{k-1}\{2(g+j)+1\}\right]\operatorname{poly}(n,\ell_{\mathrm{CRE}})\) bit operations without listing \(\binom{n}{m}\) assignments, and is therefore polynomial for every fixed \(k\). A saved constrained cluster-randomization support is a concrete conditional-design consumer, provided the endpoint is prespecified and the support is not altered after attrition.

project_justification.fill: The project proves the chamber representation and finite-sample validity, fills the completely randomized-design/ordinary-midrank fixed-\(k\) elbow with a succinct coefficient algorithm, identifies the fixed-\(k\) and variable-\(k\) computational boundary for arbitrary explicitly listed rational weights, performs exact additive-effect inversion, and gives a support-preserving constrained-cluster corollary.

prose_updates.related_work: Li, Sheng, and Yu study the same nuisance-supremum move under complete randomization with fixed potential outcomes and general treatment-indexed missingness; exchangeability together with their deterministic unit-index tie-breaking convention yields an extreme-completion closed form. Their tie convention does not settle the ordinary-midrank problem addressed here. The crossed regime distinction is: complete randomization plus index-resolved ties gives the Li--Sheng--Yu closed form; complete randomization plus ordinary midranks gives equality-inclusive chamber enumeration with polynomial coefficient evaluation at each leaf; arbitrary explicit rational weights plus ordinary midranks gives the present \(\mathrm{XP}\)/NP-complete frontier; and uniform generated restricted supports remain open. Heng, Zhang, and Feng develop imputation-assisted randomization tests that impute once and re-impute under each reassignment, prove finite-population-exact validity under their missingness mechanism, and construct finite-population-valid confidence regions. Their re-imputation law does not evaluate the supplied-design Wilcoxon-midrank completion envelope over \(\mathcal C_\delta(a)\). Zeng, Adams, and Bodenham establish arbitrary-missing Wilcoxon bounds and identify tie-induced failures of statistic-only p-value reasoning under the ordinary two-sample law. Luo, Dasgupta, Xie, and Liu establish finite Fisher validity and inversion for fully specified assignment mechanisms with complete evaluability. Sills provides exact tied-rank computation for a fixed completed sample, while Mehta, Patel, and Wei show that restricted randomization can support specialized exact recursions. Karp supplies the polynomial-reduction framework and \(\textsc{Clique}\) source problem used for the explicit-support lower bound. Hennessy et al. justify ex ante conditional randomization partitions, and Yu et al. document the saved constrained space and the distinct residual-contrast \(\texttt{cptest}\) workflow.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The completely randomized-design result is an algorithmic transfer only: it gives succinct fixed-\(k\) evaluation with ordinary midranks and equality faces. No hardness conclusion for complete randomization, uniform supports, uniform balance-generated restricted supports, or fixed-dimensional balance rules follows from the rationally weighted explicit-support reduction, whose unequal weights are load-bearing. The explicit-support fixed-\(k\) bound is \(\mathrm{XP}\), and whether an \(\mathrm{FPT}\) algorithm exists remains open. Li--Sheng--Yu's complete-randomization closed form uses index-resolved tie-breaking and is not substituted for the ordinary-midrank chamber problem. The constrained-cluster result describes a new prespecified-endpoint rank option; it does not validate unchanged \(\texttt{cptest}\), survivor conditioning, respondent-only endpoints, or conditioning on the selected assignment row. As a direct implementation sanity check, \(k=0\) reduces to the ordinary weighted Fisher test; at a singleton support or when the realized-row mass exceeds \(\alpha\), power can be vacuous.

statement_notes.justification: The explicit-support bound locates the small-attrition tractable regime by evaluating every supplied weighted row, while the companion completely randomized-design theorem removes exponential row expansion through coefficient evaluation at each chamber leaf.
statement_notes.gap: Sills computes a fixed tied-rank distribution, and Mehta, Patel, and Wei exploit special design recursions; neither combines completion weak-order enumeration with both an arbitrary supplied-weight row evaluator and a succinct completely randomized-design coefficient evaluator under ordinary midranks.
statement_notes.consumer: Small-attrition trials can compute the exact robust p-value rather than search over completions by Monte Carlo: listed restricted designs use row scans, while complete randomization uses the succinct subset-sum coefficient table.
